items.headline: CISA adds SonicWall SonicOS MFA bypass flaw to exploited vulnerabilities list
items.summary: The Hacker News: CISA placed a SonicWall SonicOS authentication-bypass issue into its exploited vulnerabilities catalog after reports of possible real-world abuse. The notice indicates defenders should treat the flaw as urgently exposed even though the public details remain limited. Help Net Security: SonicWall has patched an SSL-VPN flaw reported as actively exploited that can let attackers bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication when the feature is enabled. Administrators are being urged to patch quickly because no workaround is listed in the source. The report does not name affected organizations or confirm the scale of exploitation.
items.importance_rationale: A KEV addition for widely deployed security infrastructure indicates active concern for real-world exploitation and urgent patching.
items.detection_coverage_note: No rule URLs were provided. Defenders should look for anomalous SonicWall admin access, unexpected session establishment, and configuration changes.
items.recommended_action: Patch or mitigate SonicWall SonicOS immediately, audit exposed devices, and review authentication and admin activity for signs of abuse. Help Net Security: Patch SonicWall appliances immediately, verify SAML-enabled SSL-VPN configurations, and hunt for anomalous VPN logins or session reuse tied to alternate authentication methods.
